instructions: Fill a large pot with water for the noodles and bring it to a boil. In a second pot, bring the 10 cups vegetable broth to a boil.
Meanwhile, finely chop the scallions. That should be about 4 tbsp.
Set out 4 big bowls. Put 1 tbsp oil, 2 tbsp light soy sauce, 1/4 tsp dark soy sauce and 1/4 tsp sugar in each one.
Cook the noodles as the package says, until they're just tender with a little bite left. Drain them well.
Pour 2 1/2 cups of the hot broth into each bowl and stir. Divide the noodles between the bowls and sprinkle the scallions over the top.
Taste the broth. If it's flat, add a pinch of salt. Serve right away.
method_notes: The lead is Cup of Yum (4.9 from 52 reviews), which is the same recipe as The Woks of Life's yang chun noodle soup. The Woks of Life page shows no rating. Both build the bowl the same way: light soy, a little dark soy, sugar and fat in the bowl, then hot broth, thin noodles and scallion. They use 1 tbsp of lard per bowl and chicken broth; this uses vegetable oil and vegetable broth instead, since the list promises a vegetarian bowl. The amounts are for one bowl in the lead, so they are multiplied by 4 here.
